The region enclosed by the curves $x=\frac{5y}{8}$ and $x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}$ is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the line $x=-2.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =\frac{5y}{8} \\ 2{y}^{2} & =5y \\ 2{y}^{2}-5y & =0 \\ y(2y-5) & =0 \\ y & =0,\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=\frac{5}{2}.$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/504e204d73a1f87d72a321e7c0f58eadf01840ff3b8dbc5214f08e50fcbdcf9b.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{4},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=\frac{5}{8}y.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=\frac{5}{8}y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/0c43a01a8548112d8dc1f30f9059c560ac7bec1e679a6c76394d83e4bfbea668.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}{[\,(\frac{5}{8}y)-(-2)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}{[\frac{5}{8}y+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/d8478ef13983e6529fa10147f9659171e31a5555cb799ec1fad13d1fe8b25191.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}{[\,(\frac{{y}^{2}}{4})-(-2)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}{[\frac{5}{8}y+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}y-\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5/2}({[\frac{5}{8}y+2]}^{2}-{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+2]}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
